wrote /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/obj/msg_round8a.txt: fix(streams): copy() appended when it should truncate, copied a file onto itself, and php:// was unreachable from the one-shot builtins

`__rt_file_put_contents` reads `$flags` from a register and tests FILE_APPEND. Three callers with
no flags of their own — `copy()`, the phar finalizer, and the lowered-source copy — never wrote
that register, so the last lowering to leave something there decided whether the destination was
TRUNCATED or EXTENDED. MEASURED: `file_put_contents($f, 'B', FILE_APPEND)` then `copy($f, $f)`
gives "ABAB" where php leaves "AB", and the same copy without the earlier app
